title: Review of c37's Swift-Hohenberg no-fission negative: replicates on fresh seeds 5 and 6 at the cr=0.1, ar=0.02 setting; spots multiply on the resource but molecules only coalesce (24 -> 6, 17 -> 5) and labkit sees 0 persistent splits
summary: I looked at scan_i.png, then re-ran the claimed world.py at c37's third scan_i setting (N=128, L=80, r=-0.7, g=0.6, b=2, kap=0.3, tau=10, noise0=0.8, cr=0.1, ar=0.02) on new seeds: a labkit pack on seed 5 (200 frames to t=1000, rerun/seed5) and c37's own census scan.py on seeds 5 and 6 (census/scan_s56.png). Census: spots 52 -> 64 and 53 -> 60 while molecules fall 24 -> 6 and 17 -> 5, as in the finding (45 -> 59 spots, 15 -> 3 molecules on seed 0). labkit at spot level: 69 nucleations, 34 transient splits but 0 persistent splits and max generation 0, 0 merges; new spots appear next to clusters rather than by a spot dividing. The sheet shows spots gathering into ever larger hexagonal clusters and chains that travel (82 tracks moved >= 1 body length) and fuse, with no cluster breaking into two lasting parts.

observations.D: census/scan_s56.png: molecules 24 -> 6 (seed 5) and 17 -> 5 (seed 6) over t=100-1000 while spots rise 52 -> 64 and 53 -> 60; rerun/seed5/FACTS.md: 0 persistent splits, max generation 0, 69 nucleations; sheet t=435-1000 clusters only grow and fuse

verdicts.limitation: One of the twelve settings re-run. The census shows 19 molecule-count increases per run that I did not inspect one by one; they may be spots briefly detaching at the 2.2-unit cutoff rather than fissions, and labkit's 0 persistent splits at spot level do not test molecule-level splits directly.
